correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite, exhaustive theorem on the standard 27-vertex Schläfli graph. The attached verifier constructs adjacency from two independent representations (intersection form and double-six rules), checks all 27 vertex degrees and all 351 pairwise common-neighbor counts, independently computes traces for all 1+27+351+2925+17550 supports of size at most four, tests the iff-edge/triangle/clique criteria for every support, and checks 12 top-face orbits. Cardinality 27<32 rules out larger support. Every step was independently executed and reviewed from the actual embedded checker path; no extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The primary 2024 paper develops a general closed-neighborhood VC-dimension algorithm, not an exact Schläfli shattering complex; the 2023 pseudorandom-graph paper gives asymptotic open-neighborhood dimension bounds, not finite support characterizations. Classical Schläfli geometry supplies the graph and clique counts, but the complete open/closed trace requirements and the asymmetric degree-three support classification are additional. Database and exact-phrase searches exposed no stronger statement implying both full polynomials. The published related 27-line collinearity graph result concerns a different complex. Historical priority under alternative terminology is a residual risk.
residual_risks: A historical combinatorial classification might describe the same trace structure using the 27-line configuration, GQ(2,4), or coding terminology without VC language.

value.rationale: For the canonical 27-line cubic-surface graph, the full shattering complex is a natural learning invariant not reduced to the scalar VC dimension or classical clique counts. The result exposes a sharp open-versus-closed phenomenon: both classes have identical 1080 top-dimensional four-cliques, while their shattered triples differ by 2160, and gives uniform induced-subgraph characterizations for all support sizes. These exact natural invariants clarify which local incidence configurations support arbitrary traces, providing motivated structural information beyond a routine single-number computation.
